assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors turn a defined chemical reaction (cytidine and adenosine deamination on a displaced DNA strand) into a general tool for single-nucleotide correction of the genome. The concept is original, mechanistically clear and already used preclinically and clinically, with obvious value for anyone studying how point mutations arise and are repaired.
assessment.attribution: Liu led both the cytosine and adenine base editor programs; Komor (BE1-BE3) and Gaudelli (ABE, with the evolved TadA deaminase) were the lead experimentalists. A Liu-Komor-Gaudelli configuration is defensible, though a prize could also go to Liu alone or be combined with prime editing. Credit for the earlier Kondo/Nishida deaminase-fusion work is real but secondary.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced in many labs and organisms, with first clinical data. Timely, though long-term safety (off-target deamination, bystander edits) is still being established.
uncertainties: Whether the committee prefers to treat base and prime editing as one Liu-centred discovery or to recognise other genome-editing work first.
Long-term clinical safety and durability of benefit remain unproven.
The Kondo/Nishida contribution may be underweighted if only three names are allowed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Sequencing-by-synthesis with reversible terminators and clustered arrays reduced the cost of reading genomes by orders of magnitude and transformed biology and medicine. It rests on genuinely chemical inventions (nucleotide chemistry, polymerase handling, surface chemistry), which is what I look for in a biological phenomenon turned into a defined reaction.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman are the clear originators of the Solexa chemistry. The longlist also credits Rothberg, Mayer and Ju, whose pyrosequencing, colony and terminator-chemistry work was parallel or earlier. A two-person prize is the cleanest, but the allocation versus 454 and other platforms is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Overwhelmingly mature: two decades of routine use and validation. Recognition is arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Dispute over priority among platform developers (Solexa, 454, Mayer, Ju).
Whether the committee sees this as chemistry or as biotechnology and medicine.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Hijacking the ubiquitin-proteasome system to degrade chosen proteins changes how drugs act, from occupancy inhibition to event-driven removal. The thalidomide-cereblon mechanism gave a concrete chemical explanation for molecular glues, and degraders are in clinical trials.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies conceived and demonstrated the original PROTAC, Handa identified cereblon as the thalidomide target, and Ciulli, Gray and others extended the field. Five or more credible names, so a three-person cut is difficult and unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent confirmation of the mechanism; clinical efficacy is still emerging, so recognition could be seen as slightly early.
uncertainties: Large number of strong contributors versus the three-person limit.
No approved PROTAC drug yet.
Weighting of the molecular-glue (thalidomide) strand against the PROTAC strand.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Shokat showed that a mutant-specific cysteine in KRAS G12C can be targeted covalently, breaking the idea that KRAS is undruggable, and earlier developed analogue-sensitive kinases as a chemical genetics tool. A well-defined chemical principle with major medical impact in oncology.
assessment.attribution: Attribution to Shokat is clear and singular for the covalent KRAS work; the subsequent drugs (sotorasib, adagrasib) came from industry and build on his finding, which could complicate a shared prize.
assessment.maturity: Approved drugs and numerous independent validations make this mature; the field is still moving on resistance.
uncertainties: Whether a single-laureate prize is acceptable and how to weigh the industry drug development.
Acquired resistance limits clinical durability.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantitative mass-spectrometry proteomics lets one measure thousands of proteins and modifications, including nucleotide-metabolism enzymes, in a single experiment. Methods are broadly enabling for biochemistry and medicine and have a measurement-first character that I value.
assessment.attribution: Mann (high-resolution quantitative and SILAC-type proteomics), Aebersold (targeted and SRM/SWATH methods) and Yates (shotgun/MudPIT) are the central figures; Hunt and Gygi also contributed decisively. Selection among them is disputed, and part of the area overlaps with the 2002 ESI/MALDI prize.
assessment.maturity: Mature and widely reproduced; however the field is a broad family of methods rather than one discovery.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2002 prize and with native MS and Orbitrap candidates.
Diffuse credit among six names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Activity-based protein profiling uses reactive probes to read out enzyme activity rather than abundance in complex proteomes, linking chemistry directly to function and drug discovery. A generalisable tool for biologists and a platform for covalent ligand discovery.
assessment.attribution: Cravatt is the principal originator of the approach in its modern form; Bogyo, Overkleeft and Weerapana made significant extensions. A single-name or small prize is plausible.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted for more than two decades, with clinical translation still moderate.
uncertainties: Whether the committee regards it as sufficiently distinct from covalent-ligand and chemoproteomic strands.
Credit to Bogyo and Overkleeft.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery that m6A in mRNA is reversible and read by dedicated proteins established an epitranscriptomic regulatory layer, with a clear chemical modification and enzymes (writers, erasers, readers). The chemistry-of-life angle is strong, and disease relevance is considerable.
assessment.attribution: He identified FTO as an m6A demethylase and framed the reversible system; Jaffrey, Dominissini and Rechavi developed transcriptome-wide mapping. The Jia, Meyer and Yang contributions complicate credit.
assessment.maturity: Substantial independent confirmation, but several mapping results and stoichiometry claims remain debated, so I judge the field less mature than the others.
uncertainties: Disputed accuracy of antibody-based m6A maps and of some functional claims.
Credit split across mapping versus mechanism contributions.
Possible overlap with prior RNA modification work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation offers a physical-chemical framework for how cells organise biochemical reactions without membranes, and it has reshaped cell biology and the study of neurodegeneration.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne demonstrated liquid-like P granules; Rosen showed phase separation of defined multivalent proteins. Pappu and Mittag contributed physical theory. A three-person split is plausible but contested.
assessment.maturity: Impact is large but physiological relevance of many reported condensates is still contested, and I would want stronger quantitative, reproducible evidence before recognition.
uncertainties: Debate over whether many condensates are functional or in vitro artefacts.
Whether this is chemistry versus physiology or medicine.
Credit among five names.
